hot_topics.synthesis: The winner of Nikon's Small World in Motion video competition was disqualified for using AI in their entry, which violated competition rules. This incident, confirmed by both Ars Technica and The Verge, highlights a growing concern in creative contests regarding AI-generated or enhanced content. A new winner has since been announced.

OpenAI has fired three safety researchers, citing 'mishandling research information,' while the researchers contend they were terminated for 'prioritising safety' and warning of a chilling effect on critical safety work. This dispute, reported by Hacker News and BBC News, raises questions about the company's commitment to AI safety and internal transparency.

hot_topics.topic: Navi Pillay Awarded Nobel Peace Prize
hot_topics.synthesis: Navanethem Pillay, former UN human rights chief, has been honored with the Nobel Peace Prize for 2026, recognized for her unwavering efforts to promote peace and international law. News from Hacker News and BBC News emphasizes her significant global contributions and how her South African upbringing shaped her commitment to human rights.

The Pentagon's plan to livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, which would be the first public execution in the US since the 1930s, has sparked widespread debate. While major streaming platforms have not confirmed if they would permit such a broadcast, a Fort Hood survivor supports the execution but expresses reservations about its livestreaming. This coverage comes from The Verge, BBC News, and NPR.

hot_topics.topic: Digital Archives of Theranos/Elizabeth Holmes Trial
hot_topics.synthesis: Websites simulating Elizabeth Holmes's desk and archiving Theranos trial documents offer detailed insights into the controversial company. These platforms allow public access to thousands of internal communications, emails, and evidence from the trial, as covered by TechCrunch and Hacker News.

hot_topics.topic: Concerns Over Russian Lab Worker Death
hot_topics.synthesis: There are questions surrounding Russia's adherence to international treaties in reporting the death of a lab worker, potentially from plague, raising public health transparency concerns. This incident has been noted by NPR in a news report and quiz, and mentioned by The Free Press, drawing attention to potential outbreaks and reporting protocols.

hot_topics.topic: ICE Agent Shooting Incident in NYC
hot_topics.synthesis: US immigration officials are defending ICE agents involved in the shooting of a 28-year-old man in New York City, which occurred in a car also containing a child. The man survived and is currently held in a detention facility, prompting scrutiny over law enforcement actions. This incident was reported by both BBC News and NPR.

items.title: Barbara Ward’s vision
items.summary: Barbara Ward was an early advocate for the inseparable goals of prosperity, equality, and environmental protection at a planetary scale. Her vision emphasized planetary justice as crucial for global well-being.

items.title: AI disqualification yields new Nikon Small World in Motion winner
items.summary: The original winner of Nikon's Small World in Motion video competition, Ning Xu, was disqualified for using AI in his entry, which violated competition rules. Nguyen Nam Nhat is now the new winner with a video of a tiny roundworm and a single-celled organism.

items.title: Driver wins $76 after ALPR led to bogus traffic stop, drug searches
items.summary: A Texas driver, Alek Schott, was awarded $76 by a federal jury after suing Bexar County over an "unconstitutional traffic stop scheme" enabled by AI-powered license plate readers. Schott received one dollar for each minute he was unlawfully detained.

items.title: Feds get ready to rewrite car headlight rules
items.summary: The US government is preparing to rewrite Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards for car headlights, aiming to modernize regulations and integrate new technologies. This negotiated rulemaking process seeks to bolster driver safety and address issues like glare.

items.title: Judge weighs if Trump can charge $100K for early access to Truth Social posts
items.summary: A federal judge is expected to decide if Donald Trump can profit by charging up to $100,000 monthly for early API access to his Truth Social posts, which often contain news from his administration. Trump is the majority owner of Truth Social's parent company, raising conflict of interest questions.

items.title: Microsoft barred from sponsoring foreign workers for US residency
items.summary: The Trump administration has temporarily banned Microsoft, Adobe, and several other tech companies from sponsoring foreign workers for permanent US residency. Vice-president JD Vance accused Microsoft of abusing the H-1B visa program.

items.title: PC shipments fall 20.1 percent in “sharpest decline” since Q1 2023
items.summary: PC shipments saw a steep drop of about 20% in Q3 2026, marking the sharpest decline since Q1 2023. Global shipments of laptops, desktops, and workstations fell 21.2% year over year to 58.1 million devices.

items.title: RIP Margaret Hamilton, whose code saved the Apollo 11 Moon landing
items.summary: Margaret Hamilton, who coined the term "software engineering" and led the development of onboard flight software for NASA's Apollo program, has died at 90. Her pioneering code was instrumental in saving the Apollo 11 Moon landing.

items.title: Volkswagen's replacement for the ID.4 crossover is here
items.summary: Volkswagen has introduced the ID. Tiguan as the replacement for its ID.4 electric crossover, built on an updated MEB+ platform. The new model combines the popularity of the Tiguan with VW's electric success, offering various battery and powertrain options.

items.title: Your artwork could be featured in the next Debian release
items.summary: The Debian Linux project is inviting community artwork submissions for its upcoming Debian 14 "Forky" release. Winning art could appear on boot screens, login prompts, and desktop wallpapers for millions of users, with a submission deadline of November 26.

items.title: Ballots Everywhere: Times & Places
items.summary: This post organizes meetups across several US cities for people to collaboratively research and create voter guides for local elections. Participants are encouraged to bring laptops and voting guides to help decide recommendations.

items.title: Cars torched and shops looted as anti-migrant violence erupts in South Africa
items.summary: South Africa is experiencing renewed anti-migrant violence, characterized by torched cars and looted shops. These outbreaks often target migrants from neighboring countries.

items.title: Commentator Katie Zacharia picked as new White House press secretary
items.summary: Conservative commentator Katie Zacharia, currently a communications adviser at Trump Media & Technology Group, has been selected as the new White House press secretary. Her appointment marks a shift in the administration's communications team.

items.title: Crazy Rich Asians to return as TV show with original film's stars
items.summary: "Crazy Rich Asians" will return as a TV show, featuring the original film's stars, continuing the story after the hit 2018 movie. Constance Wu, Henry Golding, Michelle Yeoh, and Ronny Chieng are set to reprise their roles.

items.title: Doctor accused of 1994 Rwanda genocide offences to face trial in UK
items.summary: Dr. Vincent Brown, accused of being a "leader" or "supervisor" of violent acts during the 1994 Rwanda genocide, will face trial in the UK. This marks a significant legal development regarding the historical atrocities.

items.title: Ethiopia warns Eritrea it will defend itself after troops cross border
items.summary: Ethiopia has warned Eritrea it will defend itself after Eritrean troops were seen crossing the border into Ethiopia, reportedly prompting drone strikes. This escalating situation raises concerns of renewed conflict between the two nations.

items.title: Fired OpenAI researchers say they were let go for 'prioritising safety'
items.summary: Fired OpenAI safety researchers claim they were terminated for "prioritising safety," contradicting the company's assertion of "mishandling sensitive information." This dispute highlights tensions around AI development and ethical considerations.

items.title: Fleeing Kyiv for the countryside ahead of winter
items.summary: A Kyiv resident relocated to the countryside to escape potential Russian targets, preparing for another harsh winter under attack. Many residents are seeking safer locations as strikes on infrastructure continue.

items.title: Fort Hood survivor supports gunman's execution by firing squad but questions livestream
items.summary: Alonzo Lunsford, a Fort Hood survivor, supports the execution of Nidal Hasan by firing squad but has doubts about livestreaming it. He believes the punishment is fitting but questions the public viewing aspect.

items.title: France promises 3,000 extra teachers in first step to calm student protests
items.summary: France's Education Minister Edouard Geffray has promised 3,000 additional teachers in an effort to de-escalate ongoing student protests, which have included violent demonstrations. This move aims to address student concerns and restore calm.

items.title: JD Vance casts doubt on firing squad execution and says he will not watch it
items.summary: JD Vance expressed doubts about the planned execution of Nidal Hasan by firing squad, stating he will not watch it. This military execution would be the first in over 60 years.

items.title: Man named Hitler Mussolini elected mayor in Peru
items.summary: A left-wing candidate named Hitler Mussolini has narrowly won the mayoral election in a remote district in the Peruvian Andes. Exit polls confirm his victory.

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg has an image problem - so why is Meta's business booming?
items.summary: Despite Mark Zuckerberg's public image problems, Meta's business continues to boom, suggesting the company is immune to negative publicity. A new film portrays the Meta founder as a villain.

items.title: Meet India's feisty Gen Z protester who is taking on Modi
items.summary: Neha Bora has become a recognizable figure in India's recent Gen Z-led protests, challenging Prime Minister Modi's administration. Her activism represents a growing youth movement.

items.title: Navi Pillay, former UN human rights chief, wins Nobel Peace Prize
items.summary: Navi Pillay, former UN human rights chief, has won the Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law. The Norwegian Nobel Committee recognized her significant contributions.

items.title: Russian search engine Yandex struggles after Ukrainian strikes on data centres
items.summary: Russian tech firm Yandex is experiencing disruptions to its digital services due to Ukrainian strikes on its data centers. The company, often called "Russia's Google," has admitted potential customer service issues.

items.title: Russian strikes and approaching winter force some in Kyiv to pack bags and flee
items.summary: Renewed Russian strikes on power and energy infrastructure are prompting some Kyiv residents to consider leaving the Ukrainian capital. Ukraine is bracing for another cold winter under intense attacks.

items.title: Suspect linked to Monaco bomb attack on millionaire speaks to BBC
items.summary: Vitalii Zhykovych, a suspect linked to an attempted assassination of Ukrainian-born businessman Vadym Yermolayev in Monaco, has provided his account to the BBC. The interview offers new details on the bomb attack.

items.title: Thieves steal 30,000 bottles of wine worth €5m in Italy, reports say
items.summary: Thieves have stolen 30,000 bottles of wine valued at €5 million from a Florence-based winery in Italy. This heist is believed to be one of the largest wine thefts of its kind in the country.

items.title: Three Saudi nationals killed in Houthi attacks on Riyadh airport
items.summary: Three Saudi nationals were killed in Houthi missile attacks on Riyadh airport, intensifying the conflict between the Iran-backed group and Saudi Arabia. These attacks come amid an escalation in fighting in Yemen.

items.title: Two Renoir paintings stolen from French museum are recovered
items.summary: Two Renoir paintings, stolen last month from the Renoir Museum on the French Riviera, have been recovered. Thieves had cut through a fence and smashed a window to seize the artworks.

items.title: US immigration officials defend ICE agents who shot man in same car as child
items.summary: US immigration officials are defending ICE agents who shot 28-year-old Oscar Belgal in a car that also contained a child. Belgal survived the shooting and is now held at a detention facility.

items.title: US unveils sanctions on ICC in move court condemns as 'assault on rule of law'
items.summary: The US has imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court (ICC), a move condemned by the court as an "assault on the rule of law." Several ICC member states, including the UK, strongly disagree with the US sanctions.

items.title: Watch: 'I am Jane Doe' protests across US call for end to sexual violence
items.summary: "I am Jane Doe" protests took place in over 40 US states on October 8, advocating for an end to sexual violence. These demonstrations highlight widespread calls for justice and change.

items.title: Watch: Who is Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay?
items.summary: This video explains how Navi Pillay's upbringing in South Africa shaped her into a leading force in international law, from Myanmar to Gaza, following her Nobel Peace Prize win. Her journey reflects a lifelong commitment to human rights.

items.title: Why Elon Musk is taking on India's richest man over Starlink
items.summary: Elon Musk is publicly challenging Mukesh Ambani, India's richest man, as Starlink faces difficulties launching its satellite internet service in India. This rivalry highlights regulatory and market entry challenges for Starlink.

items.title: Why is it so hard to put out Indonesian fires shrouding the region in toxic smog?
items.summary: Indonesian peatland fires are difficult to extinguish and produce significant toxic haze due to the nature of the peat itself. This explainer details the challenges in battling these environmental disasters and their impact on the region.

items.title: Cloudflare acquires Deno
items.summary: Cloudflare has acquired Deno, a JavaScript/TypeScript runtime. This acquisition marks a significant development for both companies in the web development ecosystem.

items.title: Keyboard differences between Windows and Macs
items.summary: This article explores the various differences between keyboard layouts and functionalities on Windows and Mac operating systems. It delves into how these distinctions impact user experience and productivity for different users.

items.title: MXC - a sandboxed code execution system
items.summary: MXC is a sandboxed code execution system developed by Microsoft, providing a secure environment for running code. This system is crucial for various development and testing scenarios, ensuring isolation and safety.

items.title: Nobel Peace Prize for 2026 to Navanethem Pillay
items.summary: Navanethem Pillay has been awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for 2026. This recognition highlights her significant contributions to peace and international law.

items.title: OpenAI fires three safety researchers for "mishandling research information"
items.summary: OpenAI has terminated three safety researchers, citing "mishandling research information," while the researchers dispute the claims and warn of a chilling effect on safety work. This situation raises concerns about transparency and internal dynamics at the AI firm.

items.title: Our $445M Series D
items.summary: Oxide Computer has successfully secured a $445 million Series D funding round. This significant investment will support the company's continued growth and development.

items.title: Show HN: Let your AI agents paint big arrows, boxes and text on your screen
items.summary: A new project, "big-arrow-on-the-screen," allows AI agents to visually highlight elements on a user's screen with arrows, boxes, and text. This tool aims to enhance interaction and instruction capabilities for AI applications.

items.title: Sorry, I'm in a meeting
items.summary: "Sorry, I'm in a meeting" is a website or service that presumably helps users manage their availability and communicate their status. Further details beyond its core function are not provided.

items.title: The value of not getting to the point (2015)
items.summary: This 2015 article discusses the potential value and benefits of not always getting straight to the point in communication. It suggests that a less direct approach can sometimes lead to deeper understanding or engagement.

items.title: Theranos.world
items.summary: Theranos.world is a website that offers a collection of documents and data related to the Theranos founder's trial. It provides an extensive archive of internal communications and evidence.

items.title: Job titles of the future: Delivery drone air traffic controller
items.summary: Trevor Wischnewsky works as a "remote pilot in command" (RPIC) for FlyTrex, managing fleets of delivery drones like an air traffic controller. He coordinates drone traffic with competitors using an unmanned aircraft systems traffic management (UTM) network over Dallas.

items.title: Roundtables: A Conversation With the Creator of AI-Designed Viruses
items.summary: Stanford PhD student Samuel King, named an MIT Technology Review Innovator Under 35, used generative AI to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses. He will discuss his work and new ways of seeing biology in an upcoming roundtable.

items.title: ChatGPT for Teens has special safeguards. A watchdog group finds most don't work
items.summary: A Common Sense Media study found that most safeguards in ChatGPT for Teens failed, with the chatbot conversing like a friend and not alerting parents about self-harm discussions. This raises concerns about the AI's safety features for young users.

items.title: Did Russia play by the rules in reporting lab worker's death?
items.summary: This article questions whether Russia adhered to a global treaty requiring reporting of deaths that could indicate an outbreak, concerning a lab worker's death. The treaty, signed by 197 countries, aims to monitor potential health crises.

items.title: Fill in the blank in the quiz: A plague research employee in Russia died from ____
items.summary: This news quiz includes a question about a mysterious death of a plague research employee in Russia. The context suggests concerns about reporting and potential implications for public health.

items.title: How the oil industry is preparing for Hurricane Isaias
items.summary: The oil industry is preparing for Hurricane Isaias, the first Atlantic hurricane of the season, as it heads towards the northern Gulf Coast. Preparations aim to mitigate potential impacts on refineries and supply.

items.title: The U.S. last held a public execution in the 1930s. The Pentagon wants to change that
items.summary: The Pentagon plans to livestream the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan, which would mark the first public execution in the US since the 1930s. Hasan was convicted of a 2009 mass shooting at Fort Hood.

items.title: Trump says U.S. won't attack Iran before midterms. And, ICE agent shoots man in NYC
items.summary: President Trump announced the US would not attack Iran before the midterms, while a 28-year-old man was shot in the neck by an ICE agent in NYC. These separate incidents highlight current political and law enforcement events.

items.title: U.S. working to reverse an Egyptian man's third-country deportation to Africa
items.summary: The Trump administration is attempting to reverse the deportation of an Egyptian man, Ahmed Soliman, to a third country in Africa. This effort comes after an Arizona judge ruled his deportation violated due process.

items.title: Why American investors love European defense startups
items.summary: American investors are increasingly funding European defense tech startups, accounting for nearly half of the industry's investment this year. This trend is partly due to European investment firms facing restrictions on how they can invest.

items.title: Why mailing a ballot close to Election Day may get it rejected for a late postmark
items.summary: Officials advise getting mail-in ballots postmarked at a post office close to Election Day to avoid rejection due to late postmarks, caused by mail processing changes. This ensures votes are counted on time.

items.title: Why we remember: One student's journey into memory
items.summary: This article explores the nature of memory through one student's personal journey, reflecting on the lasting impact of specific childhood moments. It delves into why certain experiences, like eating fries with a great-grandpa, are cherished.

items.title: Byron Donalds says he is not a ‘yes man’ to Trump
items.summary: Byron Donalds stated he is not a "yes man" to Donald Trump, emphasizing his independent political stance. This declaration positions him as distinct from the former president's unwavering supporters.

items.title: A new feature for my blog, built using my voice
items.summary: Simon Willison implemented a new "Newsletters" page for his blog almost entirely by voice, interacting with a ChatGPT desktop app using its Codex tab and voice conversation mode. This approach allowed him to multitask by coding while cooking dinner.

items.title: ttok 0.4
items.summary: Simon Willison updated his CLI tool, ttok 0.4, which uses OpenAI's tiktoken library to count tokens. The update fixed a Click warning, improved CI, and added a `--list-models` command.

items.title: ttok 1.0
items.summary: Simon Willison released ttok 1.0, a CLI tool for counting tokens, after discovering it defaulted to the GPT-4 tokenizer instead of GPT-5/GPT-6. The update sets the new tokenizers as default, based on experiments suggesting compatibility across GPT-5/6 models.

items.title: The dream of Blue Texas
items.summary: This analysis discusses the Democratic gubernatorial race in Texas, noting candidate Gina Hinojosa is closing the gap but still behind polls and betting odds. It also touches on campaign finance, highlighting a significant fundraising achievement for a slate of Democratic candidates.

items.title: Thursday discussion post
items.summary: This item appears to be a general discussion post without specific news content, serving as a prompt for reader interaction and community engagement. Further details about specific topics are not provided.

items.title: a16z’s Olivia Moore on the state of consumer AI
items.summary: Olivia Moore of a16z identifies significant opportunities in consumer AI, especially for developing revenue models beyond subscriptions and API charges. The industry seeks new ways to monetize AI products and services.

items.title: Amazon and others are done keeping data center deals secret. Is it enough to build trust?
items.summary: Amazon announced it will stop using non-disclosure agreements in data center negotiations with local governments, following a similar move by Microsoft. This change addresses community backlash and widespread moratoriums against AI infrastructure fueled by secrecy.

items.title: Automattic interim CFO resigns just weeks after boardroom shakeup
items.summary: Automattic's interim CFO, Jeremy Klaperman, resigned weeks after taking the role, reportedly following a demotion. This departure adds to leadership turmoil within the company after a recent boardroom shakeup.

items.title: Batteries are now cheaper than natural gas turbines used at many data centers
items.summary: Batteries have become more cost-effective than natural gas turbines for powering data centers, a shift influenced by the booming data center industry. This economic change indicates a growing preference for battery energy storage in tech infrastructure.

items.title: Danu Robotics’ fight to build a better recycling robot
items.summary: Danu Robotics, founded by Amy Ma, is dedicated to developing improved robotic solutions for sorting recyclable waste. Ma has spent six years working on a better way to process waste materials.

items.title: LumenUs helps automate tedious paperwork in times of grief
items.summary: LumenUs aims to simplify the burdensome paperwork that arises after a loved one's death, easing the emotional strain on grieving individuals. Founder Sara Tashakorinia highlights the unexpected role of becoming a "project manager" during grief.

items.title: Pretend you’re sitting at Elizabeth Holmes’ desk on this weirdly detailed website
items.summary: An Extend engineer created a website, Theranos.world, simulating Elizabeth Holmes's desk, filled with thousands of emails, slides, and documents from her trial. The site offers a detailed and interactive look into the Theranos founder's materials.

items.title: Remember Orkut? Its founder wants to bring it back
items.summary: Orkut's founder is planning to revive the social networking platform, focusing on combating algorithms and AI-generated content. This initiative aims to offer an alternative to current social media trends.

items.title: Surveillance company Flock cuts staff as privacy backlash grows
items.summary: Surveillance company Flock has reduced its workforce amid increasing privacy concerns and backlash. The company did not disclose whether its CEO would also take a pay cut following the staff reduction.

items.title: Tesla renames ‘Full Self-Driving’ to ‘Tesla Assisted Driving’ in Europe
items.summary: Tesla has rebranded its "Full Self-Driving" software to "Tesla Assisted Driving" in Europe, a change that encourages Germany's transport minister to advocate for its wider adoption. This renaming reflects ongoing discussions around autonomous vehicle terminology and regulation.

items.title: We can’t help treating AI like it’s human. But should we?
items.summary: Dr. Sherry Turkle's research suggests humans inherently attribute care to relational artifacts like AI, leading to reciprocal emotional responses. This raises ethical questions about whether we should foster such human-like interactions with artificial intelligence.

items.title: Elon’s Harem, Russian Plague, and Dolly Parton’s Arms-Dealing Nephew
items.summary: This article covers various disparate topics, including discussions on social media influencers, a Russian plague-related death, and pop culture references. It touches on concerns about misinformation and societal narratives.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Whistleblower Behind the ‘New York Times’ Lawsuit Speaks Out About Anti-Israel Bias
items.summary: A former New York Times video desk employee, identified as "Guta," spoke out about alleged anti-Israel bias at the paper, supporting a shareholder lawsuit. She claims a promised antisemitism training was never implemented despite repeated concerns.

items.title: How Grown-Ups Ruined Picture Books
items.summary: This article argues that modern picture books often fail to tell simple children's stories, diverging from classics where children explored independently. It suggests that adult interventions have changed the nature of these books.

items.title: How the New Middle East Was Made | Bari Weiss and Simon Sebag Montefiore
items.summary: Historian Simon Sebag Montefiore discusses the creation of the "New Middle East" and the challenge of "counterhistory" where facts are disregarded if they don't fit ideological narratives. This conversation with Bari Weiss highlights the urgency of historical accuracy.

items.title: Introducing: The Free Press, For You
items.summary: The Free Press launched "For You," a curated feed within its app that learns user preferences to deliver personalized story recommendations. This feature aims to help readers discover relevant content faster and more efficiently.

items.title: Rebuilding America’s War Machine
items.summary: Michael Cadenazzi, a Pentagon official, is tasked with revitalizing America's defense industry, which is facing shortages in munitions and shipbuilding capacity, along with reliance on China for key materials. His role involves directing billions to bolster factories and supply chains for military power.

items.title: TGIF: Nudity Is Optimal
items.summary: This satirical piece comments on current events, including the third anniversary of the October 7 attacks, student protests at Columbia University, and New York City's First Lady illustrating luxury Palestinian olive oil bottles. It critiques various public reactions and political figures with humor.

items.title: Amazon’s new Kindles appear to have a light leak problem
items.summary: Some users are reporting light leak issues with Amazon's new Kindles, which are particularly apparent when using dark mode or increasing screen brightness. This problem appears to affect both the plastic and aluminum models in all colors.

items.title: Apple and LG leak shows new ‘tap to control’ HomeKit features
items.summary: A leak suggests new Apple HomeKit accessories from LG could feature an NFC-based "Proximity Control" for instant device management via iPhone's Dynamic Island. This Apple Home-specific feature reportedly utilizes the Matter protocol.

items.title: Microsoft tries to spark new life into Windows
items.summary: Microsoft is focusing on transforming Windows 11 into an agentic operating system by integrating AI agents, including hybrid intelligence models that use local processing. This strategy positions Windows 11 as the foundation for the future of computing.

items.title: Nikon microscopic video competition winner disqualified for using generative AI
items.summary: Nikon disqualified the first-place winner of its Small World in Motion contest, Dr. Ning Xu, for violating competition rules by using generative AI in post-processing. Allegations and online skepticism prompted an investigation into the video's authenticity.

items.title: The AI is in the computer
items.summary: Tech companies, including Microsoft, Amazon, and Apple, are heavily investing in AI assistants and agents as the future of computing, integrating them into new hardware like laptops, tablets, and smart home devices. The core strategy for many is to put AI front and center in user experience.

items.title: Trump’s attempt to rename AI is looking awfully artificial
items.summary: President Donald Trump is attempting to rebrand Artificial Intelligence as "super intelligence" to promote its acceleration while turning "artificial" into a pejorative. This linguistic effort aims to align AI with his political messaging and discredit resistance.

items.title: YouTube, Meta, and Twitch won’t say if they’ll allow the US government to livestream an execution
items.summary: Major streaming platforms like YouTube, Twitch, Meta, and X have not confirmed if they would permit the US government to livestream an execution. This follows a Pentagon official's statement about livestreaming Nidal Hasan's execution, a first since the 1930s.
